narrative_purpose: Separates two survival strategies the prose warns readers not to confuse: resistance prevents the initial injury, while resilience accepts visible damage and restores function afterward.
subject: A two-panel fire comparison. Left panel: one massive thick-barked trunk stands in a low ground fire; flames curl around the intact bark and die without entering, while the crown remains unchanged. Right panel: an ordinary stand has already burned to black stumps and ash, but fresh green-cyan shoots, fungal threads, and young saplings are spreading densely through the scar; the damage is unmistakable and so is the recovery.
scene: Two matched forest disturbances, one stopped at the surface and one followed by vigorous ecological regrowth.
camera: Wide eye-level diptych with the resistant trunk and the regenerating burn scar at matched scale.
light: Scarce ember light marks the fire and char; cool living bioluminescence illuminates the intact crown and the new growth.
palette: Cool forest tones dominate, with ember amber confined to flame and char and vivid living teal reserved for regrowth.
style: Painterly disturbance-ecology naturalist plate, tactile bark, ash, shoots, and fungal threads.
detail_level: Crisp on bark-fire contact in the left panel and on multiple stages of new growth in the right; distant forest soft.
composition: Equal panels with a dark gutter; left has one uninjured vertical subject, right has a low horizontal carpet of recovery and open dark sky for callouts.
consistency_notes: Left must show little damage because the blow is resisted. Right must show severe damage plus unmistakable recovery; do not make resilience look like immunity.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no people, no firefighting equipment, no photographic or 3D-render look, no excessive orange area
